note: The MEASURABLE definition of a negative control. It is not the list of which negative controls apply — that list is owned by the modern-rescue manifest (a control file's calibration.negativeControls, narrowed by a family file's themeControls[].negativeControls) and is read from there at run time. This file only answers 'given that declared phrase, which computed properties must not move'. A manifest phrase with no entry here is UNRESOLVED and fails the run by name; the harness never guesses a phrase's meaning and never drops one it cannot read.

assertionVocabulary.did-not-move: The named properties must read the same value in the mutation phase as in the baseline phase. Any single moved row is a violation.

targetScopeVocabulary.every-measured-target: The claim holds everywhere, so it is checked on every measured target with no binding required.
targetScopeVocabulary.declared-targets: The claim is about a specific kind of element (a control, an icon, a numeric-gap instance), so the run MUST bind the target keys it applies to. An unbound declared-targets entry fails closed rather than silently checking nothing.

phrases: columnGap and rowGap numeric values remain exact and override main gap per CSS
finite numeric spacing remains exact and never scales
numeric and tuple size remain exact
entries.meaning: A numeric gap is exact instance geometry. Rhythm is applied at the preset rungs, never at a consume site, so an instance that asked for 8px must still read 8px.

Rhythm scales the room around a control, never the control. Bound to control-bearing targets deliberately: a LAYOUT container's intrinsic height legitimately grows when its gaps grow, so checking this everywhere would report the intended effect as a violation. Includes the indirect vectors a rule could use to change the control's rendered size without touching height/block-size directly: max-height (the physical dual of max-block-size), aspect-ratio (a fixed width plus a moved aspect-ratio moves height too), scale, zoom and contain-intrinsic-size. The two `@rect-*` reserved observables are the RENDERED box read from getBoundingClientRect, so a padding/border/transform mutation that changes what is actually painted cannot hide behind an unmoved computed longhand.

The coarse-pointer touch floor must survive every rhythm stop by construction rather than by clamping, so the hit box of a bound interactive target may not move at all. 'May not move at all' includes the ceiling as well as the floor (max-inline-size and its physical dual max-width; min-width is min-inline-size's physical dual) and the indirect vectors that resize a box without changing its own size properties: aspect-ratio, scale, zoom and contain-intrinsic-size. The two `@rect-*` reserved observables are the RENDERED box read from getBoundingClientRect, so this assertion does not depend on width/height strings alone.

Icon boxes are sized by the icon channels, not by layout rhythm. Includes the indirect vectors that could change an icon's rendered box without moving its own width/height/inline-size/block-size: aspect-ratio, scale, zoom and contain-intrinsic-size. The two `@rect-*` reserved observables are the RENDERED box read from getBoundingClientRect, so this assertion does not depend on width/height strings alone.
Rhythm is a spacing axis. It shares no channel with the type scale, so no measured element may change a font metric under it.
Rhythm shares no channel with any palette seed.
Border geometry belongs to the shape axis. Radius is included on purpose: a rhythm stop that moved a corner would be reaching a channel it does not own.

phrases: border width and style remain fixed
entries.meaning: The stroke of the border and the corner of the border are two different channels of the shape axis. `border-fixed` deliberately bundles them, which is correct for an axis that owns NEITHER -- a rhythm stop that moved a corner would be reaching outside itself. It is unusable for the radius dial itself: binding it would assert that the very channel under test must not move. This entry is `border-fixed` minus the four radius longhands, so a radius stop still has to prove it left the stroke alone. Use it INSTEAD OF `border remains fixed`, never alongside it.

phrases: direction wrap alignment width overflow font color border and motion remain unchanged
direction wrap align justify and touch ownership remain unchanged
entries.meaning: The Flex family narrows the control-level claim onto its own root: only the gap axes may move.

phrases: track templates item spans auto-flow alignment font color border and motion remain unchanged
entries.meaning: The Grid family narrows the control-level claim onto its own root.
partiallyMechanised: track templates: getComputedStyle resolves grid-template-columns/rows to USED track sizes rather than the authored template, and flexible tracks in a fixed-width container must absorb any gap change by arithmetic (measured repeat(2, minmax(0,1fr)) at 1280px: 632.5px tracks + 15px gap at normal, 631px tracks + 18px gap at airy, both exactly 1280). Asserting did-not-move on them reports the control's intended effect as a violation, for the same reason control height is not asserted on a layout container.

entries.meaning: The Stack family narrows the control-level claim onto its own root and its divider part.
